public_rationale: The study available on May 25, 2023 reported approximately 34% performance for GPT-4 on Blocksworld planning tasks, with little improvement from chain-of-thought prompting [e1]. This documented planning limitation supports the narrow claim that contemporary LLMs lacked the full range of human competence; it does not imply that they lacked all useful capabilities [e1].
limitations: The evaluation covers a bounded planning domain and specific models and prompting methods, not every dimension of intelligence.
The human comparison does not establish performance relative to trained professionals generally.
The study evaluates generated plans, not physical execution or external-tool use.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Contrary to what humans naturally imagine, LLMs are not generally intelligent in all the ways humans are, nor perfectly capable of acting on their own output in all the ways trained humans might be.

statement.excerpt: It is natural for humans to imagine LLMs to be generally intelligent in all the ways that humans are, and perfectly capable of taking their own output and acting on them in all the ways that trained humans might be able to do. In reality, they are not able to do so.
statement.document_title: Getting GPT to work with external tools is harder than you think

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that contemporary LLMs lacked the full range of human competence and could not reliably turn generated solutions into correct actions across human-manageable tasks.
This does not claim that LLMs fail every task or that humans perform perfectly.
For this ongoing technical observation, I use the 2023 evaluation cycle through publication. The post supplies no exact observation window.
The introductory statement about what humans imagine is framing, not a separate measured claim about public opinion.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary comparative evaluations document reproducible reasoning or action-planning failures on tasks that instructed humans can perform, demonstrating a material gap in the claimed range of competence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparative evidence establishes dependable human-general reasoning and execution across the claimed scope, and the apparent deficits disappear under fair testing.

evidence.locator: Section 4, Blocksworld evaluation; human baseline follows in the same section
evidence.explanation: The study tested GPT-4 between March and May and found substantial failures in generating executable plans. Its instructed human baseline produced valid plans for 39 of 50 participants, supporting a concrete competence gap without assuming human perfection.
